They do not descend except by His command, and they do nothing except after His permission. They are: ﴿honored servants﴾ [al-Anbiya': 26].

Among them are those who stand in rows and those who glorify. None of them has a station except one that is known, which he does not transgress, and he is engaged in a work he has been commanded to do, from which he does not fall short nor exceed. The highest of them are those who are in His presence: ﴿They do not refuse to worship Him, nor do they tire. They glorify Him night and day without ceasing﴾ [al-Anbiya': 19–20].

They will say, "Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 31]. So He is the One who manages the affair, by His command, permission and will, while the managing angels do it directly and by execution.

This is like how He attributes death (tawaffi) to the angels at times, as in His saying: ﴿Our messengers take his soul﴾ [al-An'am: 61], and to Himself at other times, as in His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], and similar examples.

The angels assigned to the human being, from the time he is a drop of semen until the end of his affair, have a further role for him. They are assigned to shape him, move him from stage to stage, form him, and guard him in the three layers of darkness. They also record his provision, his deeds, his term of life, his misery and his happiness. They accompany him in all his states, count his words and actions, guard him in his life, seize his soul at his death, and present it to its Creator and Originator. They are also assigned to his punishment and his bliss in the barzakh (intermediate state) and after the resurrection. They are assigned to make the instruments of bliss and punishment. They are the ones who make the believing servant firm by Allah's permission, teach him what benefits him, fight and defend him. They are his allies in this world and the Hereafter. They are the ones who see him in his dream, what he fears so that he may beware of it, and what he loves so that his heart may be strengthened and he may increase in gratitude. They are the ones who promise him good, invite him to it, forbid him from evil, and warn him against it.

Thus they are his allies, helpers, guardians, teachers, advisers, those who supplicate for him and seek forgiveness for him. They are those who send blessings upon him as long as he is in obedience to his Lord, and send blessings upon him as long as he teaches people good. They give him glad tidings of Allah's honor in his dream, at his death, and on the day of his resurrection. They make him detached from the world and eager for the Hereafter. They remind him when he forgets, energize him when he is lazy, and make him steadfast when he panics. They strive for the good of his worldly life and his Hereafter.

They are thus the messengers of Allah among His creation and His command, and His emissaries between Him and His servants. They descend with the command from Him to the regions of the world, and they ascend to Him with deeds. The heaven has creaked because of them, and it has the right to creak. There is not a space of four fingers in it except that there is an angel standing, bowing, or prostrating. Every day, seventy thousand angels enter the Bayt al-Ma'mur, and they never return to it again, the last of them being what is upon it.

The Qur'an is filled with mention of the angels, their categories, their works, and their ranks. Such as the words of the Exalted: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know." And He taught Adam the names, all of them. Then He presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful." They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise." He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?" And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," ...﴾ to the end of the story [al-Baqarah: 30–38].

And His words: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord﴾ [al-Qadr: 4].

And between these two surahs, in the surahs of the Qur'an [there is mention of the angels]. Indeed, no surah of the Qur'an is free of mention of the angels, explicitly, allusively, or by indication.

As for their mention in the prophetic hadiths, it is more abundant and well-known than can be mentioned.

For this reason, belief in the angels (peace be upon them) is one of the five foundations that are the pillars of faith: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 82, verses 10–12 (part 1 of 2):**

Section

Sin distances the servant from the King. Among its punishments is that it distances the servant from his guardian, the one most beneficial and sincere to him, the one whose happiness lies in being near him, which is the angel assigned to him. It also brings near to him his enemy, the one most deceitful toward him and most harmful to him, which is Satan. When the servant disobeys Allah, the angel moves away from him by the measure of that disobedience, so much so that a single lie causes him to move a great distance away.

In some reports: "When the servant lies, the angel moves away from him a mile because of the stench of his breath." If the angel distances himself this much because of a single lie, then what is the measure of his distance from what is greater than that and more foul?

Some of the salaf (early pious predecessors) said: "When the male is mounted (in unlawful intercourse), the earth cries out to Allah, the angels flee to their Lord, and they complain to Him of the great thing they have seen."

Some of the salaf said: "When the son of Adam rises in the morning, the angel and the devil hasten to him. If he remembers Allah, glorifies Him, praises Him and declares His oneness (tahlil), the devil is driven away and the angel takes charge of him. If he begins the day otherwise, the angel leaves him and the devil takes charge of him."

The angel continues to draw near to the servant until command, obedience and dominance belong to him. Then the angels take charge of him in his life, at his death and at his resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but rejoice in Paradise which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter"﴾ [Fussilat: 30–31].

When the angel takes charge of him, he is taken charge of by the most sincere, most beneficial and most righteous of creatures. He strengthens him, teaches him, fortifies his heart, and Allah supports him: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe"﴾ [al-Anfal: 12].

At death, the angel says: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in what will delight you." He strengthens him with the firm word, which he needs most in this worldly life, at death, and in the grave at the time of questioning.

No one is more beneficial to the servant than the companionship of the angel. He is his guardian in his wakefulness and his sleep, in his life and at his death, and in his grave. He is his companion in his loneliness, his friend in his solitude, his confidant in his secrets. He fights off his enemy for him, defends him, and helps him against him. He promises him good and gives him glad tidings of it, and urges him to affirm the truth. This is as in the report narrated as both marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and mawquf (traced to a Companion): "Indeed, the angel has an inspiration (lamma) in the heart of the son of Adam, and Satan has an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel is a promise of good and affirmation of the promise, and the inspiration of Satan is a promise of evil and denial of the truth."

When the angel draws very near to the servant, he speaks through his tongue and places upon his tongue the upright word. When he moves away and Satan draws near, Satan speaks through his tongue and places upon it false and obscene speech, until a man is seen speaking with the angel's tongue, and another speaking with Satan's tongue.

In a hadith: "Indeed, tranquility (sakinah) speaks upon the tongue of 'Umar," may Allah be pleased with him. Some of them would hear a good word from a righteous man and say, "Only the angel placed that upon your tongue." And if they heard its opposite, they would say, "Only Satan placed that upon your tongue." So the angel casts the truth into the heart and places it upon the tongue, while Satan casts falsehood into the heart and causes it to flow upon the tongue.

Among the punishments of sins is that they distance from the servant his guardian, whose happiness lies in nearness to him, in his neighborhood and in his friendship, and they bring near to him his enemy, whose misery, ruin and corruption lie in nearness to him and in his friendship. So much so that the angel defends the servant and repels for him when a foolish person insults him and reviles him. Likewise, two men once quarrelled in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). One of them began to revile the other while he remained silent. Then he spoke a word to answer his companion. The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up. He was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, when I responded to him with some of his words, you stood up?" He said: "The angel was defending you, but when you responded to him, Satan came, and I would not sit with Satan."

When a Muslim servant prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says "Amin" to his supplication and says: "And for you the same."

When he finishes reciting al-Fatihah, the angels say "Amin" to his supplication.

When a believing servant who is monotheistic and follows the way and Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) sins, the bearers of the Throne and those around it seek forgiveness for him.

If honoring the guest is among the obligations of faith for human beings, and kindness to the neighbor is among its requirements, then what is the expectation regarding honoring the most noble of guests and the best and most righteous of neighbors? ﴿And whoever God humiliates, for him there is no honorer. Indeed, God does what He wills﴾ [al-Hajj: 18].

This is known to the one who has insight, and he witnesses it in himself and in others.

and His statement: ﴿And the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-A'raf: 128; al-Qasas: 83];

and similar verses, and he is one who believes in the Qur'an, he interprets that as its fulfillment only in the Hereafter. He says: "As for this world, we see the disbelievers and hypocrites prevailing and dominating in it, and they have the victory and success."

*then what does He do to His enemies?*

And you see many people, when some kind of affliction befalls them, saying: "O my Lord, what was my sin, that You have done this to me?"

And more than one person has told me: "When I repent to Him, return to Him and do righteous deeds, my provision is restricted and my livelihood becomes hard, but when I return to His disobedience and give myself its desire, provision and help come to me," and similar things.

So I said to some of them: "This is a trial from Him, to see your truthfulness and patience: whether you are sincere in your coming to Him and turning to Him, so that you endure His affliction, and the outcome will be yours, or whether you are a liar and you turn back on your heels."

Thus the servant's happiness, the perfection of his delight and his bliss become dependent upon these five stations: his knowledge of the bliss sought and his love for it; his knowledge of the path that leads to it and his action upon it; and his patience in that.

Consider not that His statement, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾, is restricted to the bliss and the fire of the Hereafter alone. Rather, it applies in their three abodes as well: that is, the abode of this world (al-dunya), the abode of the barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection), and the abode of permanence (dar al-qarar). So these are in bliss, and those are in the fire. And is bliss anything other than the bliss of the heart? And is punishment anything other than the punishment of the heart?

And what punishment is more severe than fear, anxiety, grief, constriction of the chest, turning away from God and the Last Abode, attachment to other than God, and being cut off from God, with every valley of it having its branches?

And everything to which a person becomes attached and loves besides God, it will inflict upon him the worst of punishments.

So everyone who loves something other than God is punished by it three times in this abode. He is punished by it before attaining it, until he attains it. Then, when he attains it, he is punished by it at the moment of attaining it, through fear of losing it and its passing away, through disturbance and vexation concerning it, and through kinds of punishment in these obstructions. Then, when it is taken from him, his punishment intensifies. These are three kinds of punishment in this abode.

As for the barzakh: there is a punishment accompanied by the pain of separation, which he does not hope will return, and the pain of missing the great bliss he has lost by busying himself with its opposite, and the pain of the veil between him and God, and the pain of regret that cuts the livers. So worry, distress and grief work within their souls like the work of vermin and worms within their bodies. Indeed, their work in the souls is constant and continuous, until God returns the souls to their bodies. Then the punishment shifts to a kind that is more calamitous and more bitter.

Where is this from the bliss of one whose heart dances with joy, delight and intimacy with his Lord, longing for Him, rejoicing in His love, and tranquility in His remembrance? So much so that one of them says at the time of his death throes: "O how joyful!"

Another says: "The poor people of this world! They left it without tasting the sweetness of life in it, and without tasting the finest of what is in it."

Another says: "If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us over it with swords."

Another says: "Indeed, in this world there is a paradise; whoever does not enter it will not enter the paradise of the Hereafter."

O you who have sold his precious share for the lowest price, and been cheated in the completest manner in this transaction while he thinks he has been cheated: if you have no expertise regarding the value of the merchandise, then ask the appraisers. Oh, how strange is a commodity whose buyer is God, and whose price is the Garden of Refuge, and whose intermediary through whose hand the contract of exchange passed and who guaranteed the price on behalf of the buyer is the Messenger (ﷺ). And you have sold it at the utmost degradation, as the poet said:

*If this is the deed of a servant against himself,*
*then who after that will honor him?*

﴿And whoever God humiliates, for him there is no honorer. Indeed, God does what He wills﴾ [al-Hajj: 18].

He also said in (al-Jawab al-Kafi):

And do not think that His statement, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ is specific only to the Day of Return. Rather, these are in bliss in their three abodes, and those are in the fire in their three abodes.

And what pleasure and bliss in this world is sweeter than the righteousness of the heart, the soundness of the chest, knowledge of the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, love for Him, and acting in accordance with His pleasure? Is life in reality anything other than the life of the sound heart? God, glorified is He, praised His intimate friend (Abraham), peace be upon him, for the soundness of his heart, saying: ﴿And indeed, among those who followed his way was Abraham, when he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat: 83-84].

And he said in (al-Madarij):

The hearts of the people of innovation, of those who turn away from the Qur'an, of those heedless of God, and of the people of sin are in a hell before the Greatest Hell. And the hearts of the righteous are in bliss before the Greatest Bliss. ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13].

This applies in their three abodes; it is not specific to the Hereafter abode, although its completion, perfection and manifestation are only in the Hereafter abode. In the barzakh it is less than that, as God said: ﴿And indeed, for those who wronged is a punishment short of that﴾ [al-Tur: 47]. And He said: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" Say, "Perhaps it has drawn near for you some of what you seek to hasten"﴾ [al-Naml: 71].

And in this abode it is less than what is in the barzakh. But what prevents one from perceiving it is being absorbed in the intoxication of desires, casting it away from the heart, and not reflecting upon it.

A servant may suffer a physical pain, so he casts it from his heart, cuts off his attention from it, and directs his focus to something else, so that he does not feel it at all. Then, if that diversion of attention were removed from him, he would cry out from the intensity of the pain. So what do you think of the punishment of hearts and their pains?!

God, glorified is He, has placed for good deeds and acts of obedience effects that are beloved, delightful and pure, whose pleasure exceeds the pleasure of disobedience by manifold multiples, with no comparison between them. And He has placed for evil deeds and acts of disobedience pains and disliked effects, and aversions which exceed the pleasure of indulging in them by manifold multiples. Ibn Abbas said: "Indeed, a good deed has a light in the heart, a radiance in the face, strength in the body, increase in provision, and love in the hearts of creation. And indeed an evil deed has blackness in the face, darkness in the heart, weakness in the body, deficiency in provision, and hatred in the hearts of creation." This is known to the one who has insight, and he witnesses it in himself and in others.

No disliked state ever befalls a servant except because of a sin, and what God forgives is more. God said: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

He also said in (Ighathat al-Lahfan):

And His statement: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 13-14].

So He promised the people of guidance and righteous deeds complete bliss in the Hereafter, and threatened the people of misguidance and wickedness with misery in the Hereafter, a matter upon which all the messengers, from the first of them to the last, agreed, and which the scriptures contain.

But here we mention a beneficial point: A person may hear and see what afflicts many of the people of faith in this world of calamities, and what many disbelievers, wicked people and oppressors attain in this world of leadership, wealth and other things. So he believes that bliss in this world belongs only to disbelievers and wicked people, and that the believers' share of bliss in this world is small. Likewise, he may believe that honor and victory in this world are settled for disbelievers and hypocrites over the believers.

Then when he hears in the Qur'an His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And honor belongs to God, to His Messenger and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8];

and His statement: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173];

and His statement: ﴿God has decreed, "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21];

and His statement: ﴿And the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ [al-A'raf: 128; al-Qasas: 83];

and similar verses, and he is one who believes in the Qur'an, he interprets that as its fulfillment only in the Hereafter. He says: "As for this world, we see the disbelievers and hypocrites prevailing and dominating in it, and they have the victory and success."

But the Qur'an does not come in contradiction to what is perceived, and he relies upon this assumption when an enemy of the kind of disbelievers and hypocrites, or of the wicked oppressors, gains the upper hand over him, while he considers himself among the people of faith and piety. So he sees that the possessor of falsehood has risen over the possessor of truth, and he says: "I am upon the truth, and I am defeated." So the possessor of truth in this world is defeated and overpowered, and dominance in it belongs to falsehood.
